category: Vivado IDE: Windows, Menus, Settings & Customisation
description: The graphical side of Vivado beyond the Flow Navigator: the Getting Started page and Project Summary, the data windows (Sources, Properties, Netlist, Hierarchy, Schematic, Device, Package, Package Pins, I/O Ports, Device Constraints, Hard Block Planner, Selection), the results windows (Messages suppression and severity, Log, Reports, Timing), the Text Editor, Find dialog, Edit Device Properties and Language Templates, layouts, Tools > Settings pages, strategies and shortcuts, Run Tcl Script, custom commands, the Vivado Store / Xilinx Tcl Store / xhub board store, ELF association, Hardware Manager Auto Connect, DocNav and the Vivado License Manager.

tools.name: Getting Started page
tools.description: The start screen shown when the Vivado IDE opens with no project loaded. Quick Start offers Create Project, Open Project and Open Example Project; Tasks offers Manage IP, Open Hardware Manager and the Vivado Store; the Learning Center links documentation, tutorials and QuickTake videos; and Recent Projects / Recent Checkpoints / Recent IP Locations give one-click reopening.
tools.usage:
Shown at startup, or after File > Project > Close (all projects must be closed for it to appear).
Quick Start: Create Project | Open Project | Open Example Project
Tasks: Manage IP | Open Hardware Manager | Vivado Store
Learning Center: Documentation and Tutorials | QuickTake Videos | What's New

parameters.name: Open Example Project
parameters.description: Wizard that creates a project from shipped or store-installed examples (e.g. BFT small RTL project, CPU (HDL), CPU (Synthesized), Wavegen (HDL)); Refresh downloads the latest configurable example designs.

parameters.name: Manage IP
parameters.description: Creates or opens a Managed IP project for customising IP standalone (outside any design project).

parameters.name: Recent lists
parameters.description: Ten entries by default; change under Tools > Settings > Tool Settings > Project > Recent.

tools.example:
1. Launch vivado from the directory where logs should go.
2. Getting Started > Open Example Project > Next > choose 'Wavegen (HDL)' > set name/location > pick a part > Finish.
3. Equivalent Tcl for an ordinary project: create_project wavegen ./wavegen -part xc7a35tcsg324-1
tools.notes: Configurable example designs (e.g. MicroBlaze presets, Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC designs) are not all installed by default; they come from the Example Designs tab of the Vivado Store. Double-clicking an .xpr also opens Vivado directly on that project.

tools.name: Project Summary (Window > Project Summary)
tools.description: Interactive project overview that updates as the flow runs. The Overview tab shows part, board, synthesis/implementation status, DRC violations, timing (WNS/TNS/WHS/THS), utilisation and power with links into Messages, Reports and Settings; the Dashboard tab holds user-configured gadgets that chart or tabulate report data across runs and implementation stages.
tools.usage:
Window > Project Summary, or the Project Summary toolbar button.
Dashboard: Add Gadget > Configure Gadget (Name, Type, Run Type, Stages, View Type graph/table, Orientation, Reports, Statistics, Hide Unused Data)
Tcl: create_dashboard_gadget -name <name> -type <report_type>; set_property <prop> <value> [get_dashboard_gadgets <name>]

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Report type feeding the gadget, e.g. timing or utilization.

parameters.name: Run Type / Stages
parameters.description: Synthesis or implementation run; for implementation choose a stage (opt, place, route...) or All Stages.

parameters.name: Reports
parameters.description: One or more run reports (from the run's report strategy) supplying the data; gadgets comparing impl_1 vs impl_2 are the usual use.

tools.example:
create_dashboard_gadget -name {gadget_1} -type timing
set_property view.type graph [get_dashboard_gadgets [list {gadget_1}]]
set_property reports {impl_1#impl_1_route_report_timing_summary_0} [get_dashboard_gadgets [list {gadget_1}]]
set_property run.step all_stages [get_dashboard_gadgets [list {gadget_1}]]
tools.notes: A gadget shows 'information unavailable' when the requested report is not part of the run's Report Strategy or was reset; add the report to the strategy (Tools > Settings > Strategies > Report Strategies) and relaunch.

tools.name: Sources window (Hierarchy, IP Sources, Libraries, Compile Order views)
tools.description: Project source manager listing Design Sources, Constraints and Simulation Sources (plus Syntax Error Files, Non-Module Files, Disabled Sources and Text folders). The Hierarchy view shows modules/instances with their files and the top module; IP Sources lists every IP's generated files; Libraries groups files by HDL library; Compile Order shows the compile sequence per flow (Synthesis, Implementation, Simulation) and constraint processing order.
tools.usage: Window > Sources. Right-click menu: Source File Properties, Open File, Replace File, Copy File Into Project, Remove File From Project, Enable/Disable File, Move to Simulation/Design Sources, Move to Top/Up/Down/Bottom (Compile Order view only), Hierarchy Update, Refresh Hierarchy, Set as Top, Set Global Include, Make Active, Set as Target Constraint File, Set as Out-of-Context for Synthesis, Set Library, Set File Type, Set Used In, Edit Constraint/Simulation Sets, Add Sources, Go to Source.

parameters.name: Hierarchy Update
parameters.description: Automatic Update and Compile Order (default), Automatic Update + Manual Compile Order (all files passed to tools in the listed order), or No Update + Manual Compile Order (use Refresh Hierarchy).

parameters.name: Set as Target Constraint File
parameters.description: File that receives new constraints created from the GUI (Save Constraints writes there).

parameters.name: IP right-click
parameters.description: Customize IP, Generate/Reset Output Products, Upgrade IP, Copy IP, Enable/Disable Core Container, Open IP Example Design, IP Documentation, Report IP Status.

parameters.name: Block design right-click
parameters.description: Create HDL Wrapper, View Instantiation Template, Generate/Reset Output Products.

tools.example:
# Tcl equivalents of common Sources-window actions
set_property top top_level [current_fileset]
set_property source_mgmt_mode DisplayOnly [current_project]   ;# Automatic Update, Manual Compile Order
set_property PROCESSING_ORDER EARLY [get_files timing_clocks.xdc]
set_property target_constrs_file ./src/pins.xdc [current_fileset -constrset]
report_compile_order -fileset sources_1
tools.notes: Critical warnings raised while building the hierarchy appear at the top of the tree; the 'Show Only Missing Sources' toolbar button becomes active when a module definition or file is missing. Disabling a file keeps it in the project but removes it from compile and hierarchy.

tools.name: Properties window
tools.description: Context-sensitive property sheet for the most recently selected object; its title changes with the object (Cell Properties, Net Properties, BEL Properties, Clock Region Properties, Source File Properties, I/O Port Properties, Run Properties...). Views are object-specific (General, Properties, Connectivity, Cell Pins, Statistics...), and editable properties can be changed in place, which echoes a set_property command.
tools.usage:
Window > Properties, or right-click an object > <ObjectType> Properties.
Toolbar: Search, Collapse/Expand All, Show or Flatten All Property Hierarchies, Add Properties, Remove Properties, Show Description, Sort Properties, Previous Object / Next Object, Settings > Automatically Update.
Right-click: Add/Remove/Reset/Copy Properties, Export to Spreadsheet.

parameters.name: Automatically Update
parameters.description: When off, the window stays on the current object instead of following new selections - useful while comparing.

parameters.name: Previous Object / Next Object
parameters.description: Step back and forth through the history of selected objects.

parameters.name: Source File Properties
parameters.description: For files: Type, Library, Global Include, Enabled and Used In (synthesis/simulation/implementation).

tools.example:
# Selecting a net and editing MARK_DEBUG in the Properties window echoes:
set_property MARK_DEBUG true [get_nets {u_ctrl/state_reg[*]}]
# The same data from Tcl:
report_property [get_cells u_ctrl/state_reg[0]]
tools.notes: With multiple objects selected only the last one is shown; use Tools > Property Editor for multi-object editing. Property changes on an opened design live in memory until File > Constraints > Save.

tools.name: Property Editor (Tools > Property Editor)
tools.description: Spreadsheet-style editor for viewing and changing properties of many selected objects at once, e.g. setting IOSTANDARD on a bus of ports or comparing LOC/BEL of a group of cells. Rows are objects and columns are properties; Fill Up / Fill Down copy an edited value to the other selected cells.
tools.usage: Select objects in any window, then Tools > Property Editor. Toolbar: Fill Up, Fill Down, Add Selected Objects, Remove Selected Objects, Settings (Group Header, Autoscroll to Selected, Types, Properties). Right-click Property Options > Show Columns with Differences.

parameters.name: Fill Up / Fill Down
parameters.description: Apply the value of the edited cell to all selected cells above or below it.

parameters.name: Show Columns with Differences
parameters.description: Hide columns whose value is identical for every object, leaving only what differs.

tools.example:
1. In the I/O Ports window select all ports of bus led[7:0].
2. Tools > Property Editor.
3. Set IOSTANDARD to LVCMOS33 in the first row, Ctrl-select the column cells below, click Fill Down.
# Echoed Tcl:
set_property IOSTANDARD LVCMOS33 [get_ports [list {led[0]} {led[1]} {led[2]} {led[3]} {led[4]} {led[5]} {led[6]} {led[7]}]]
tools.notes: Objects can be dragged from other windows onto the editor. Editable text cells show a pencil icon.

tools.name: Netlist window
tools.description: Hierarchical tree of the elaborated or synthesized/implemented netlist starting at the current top: each level has a Nets folder (buses collapsed, expandable per bit) and a Leaf Cells folder of primitives, plus child hierarchical cells. Icons distinguish black boxes, Pblock-assigned cells and placed/unplaced primitives, and selection cross-probes to the Schematic and Device windows.
tools.usage:
Window > Netlist (available when an elaborated, synthesized or implemented design is open).
Right-click a cell/net: Schematic (F4), Show Hierarchy, Mark Debug, Highlight/Mark, Select Leaf Cell Parents, Assign to Pblock, <Object> Properties.

parameters.name: Leaf Cells folder
parameters.description: Primitive cells at each hierarchy level, kept separate from child modules to condense the tree.

parameters.name: Scroll to selected objects
parameters.description: Settings option (on by default) that auto-expands the tree to objects selected in other windows.

tools.notes: A hierarchical cell with no content is displayed as a black box - either intentional or the symptom of a missing file / wrong top. Marking nets for debug here is the usual first step of the netlist-insertion debug flow.

tools.name: Hierarchy window
tools.description: Graphical block view of the logic hierarchy in which each instance is drawn inside its parent and block widths reflect the device resources each module consumes. It is used during floorplanning and timing analysis to see how big a module is and how a timing path crosses hierarchy boundaries; a Tree view shows the same data top-down.
tools.usage: Right-click a cell in the Netlist (or other) window > Show Hierarchy. Toolbar: Show Tree View. Right-click a module > Select Leaf Cell Parents, then Floorplanning > Draw Pblock or Assign to Pblock.
tools.example:
1. Open Synthesized Design.
2. Netlist window: right-click top > Show Hierarchy.
3. Right-click the widest block > Select Leaf Cell Parents > Draw Pblock around a clock region.
# Tcl for the resulting Pblock:
create_pblock pb_dsp
add_cells_to_pblock pb_dsp [get_cells u_dsp_chain]
resize_pblock pb_dsp -add CLOCKREGION_X1Y2:CLOCKREGION_X1Y3
tools.notes: Unlike other windows it cannot be opened from the Window menu without a selection. Supports mouse-stroke zoom and the World view like the Device window.

tools.name: Schematic window
tools.description: Schematic view generated for selected cells, nets, ports or timing paths at any stage (elaborated RTL, synthesized or implemented). Logic can be expanded inside/outside a module, followed pin-by-pin across hierarchy, or grown with Expand Cone to flops/I/Os, to leaf cells or between two selected cells; display options add truth-table equations, fanout, setup slack, toggle rate or static probability to pins.
tools.usage:
Select objects (Netlist window, timing path, I/O Ports...) > right-click > Schematic, the Schematic toolbar button, or F4. An elaborated design opens with a top-level schematic automatically.
Toolbar: Previous/Next, Zoom In/Out/Fit, Select Area, Autofit Selection, Autohide Pins, Add, Remove, Regenerate Schematic, Settings.
Right-click: Expand/Collapse > Expand Inside | Collapse Inside | Expand Outside | Collapse Outside; Expand Cone > To Flops or I/Os | To Leaf Cells | To Selected Cells.

parameters.name: Display settings
parameters.description: Inst Equation, Fanout, Setup Slack (after a timing report), Static Probability / Toggle Rate (after Report Power), Bus Value, Elide Long Text, Bundle Nets/Cells, Split into Multiple Pages.

parameters.name: Cells / I/O Ports / Nets links
parameters.description: Links at the top of the sheet open the objects in a searchable Find Results window.

tools.example:
# Show the worst setup path as a schematic
set p [get_timing_paths -max_paths 1 -nworst 1 -setup]
show_schematic [get_cells -of_objects $p]
# GUI: Timing window > right-click path > Schematic
tools.notes: Dotted nets continue into logic not shown. Previous/Next is disabled on schematics with more than 12,000 objects. Bundle Nets keeps RTL schematics of wide buses readable.

tools.name: show_schematic / write_schematic
tools.description: Scripted access to the Schematic window: show_schematic opens (or adds objects to / removes objects from / regenerates) a schematic for the given cells, nets, pins or ports, and write_schematic saves the currently open schematic as native ASCII, PDF or SVG for documentation outside Vivado.
tools.usage:
show_schematic [-add] [-remove] [-regenerate] [-pin_pairs] [-name <window_name>] [-quiet] [-verbose] <objects>
write_schematic [-force] [-format native|pdf|svg] [-orientation portrait|landscape] [-scope current_page|visible|all] [-name <window_name>] [-quiet] [-verbose] <file>

parameters.name: -add / -remove
parameters.description: Modify an existing schematic window instead of creating a new one (same as the Add/Remove toolbar buttons).

parameters.name: -format
parameters.description: native (ASCII, reloadable), pdf or svg.

parameters.name: -scope
parameters.description: Write the current page, only the visible area, or the whole schematic.

parameters.name: -orientation
parameters.description: portrait (default) or landscape page orientation for PDF output.

tools.example:
open_run synth_1
show_schematic -name ctrl_fsm [get_cells u_ctrl/*]
write_schematic -format pdf -orientation landscape -scope all -name ctrl_fsm ./doc/ctrl_fsm.pdf -force
tools.notes: Both need the GUI (start_gui) because they operate on a schematic window; they have no effect in pure batch mode.

tools.name: Device window
tools.description: Main graphical view of the target die used for floorplanning and physical analysis: clock regions, I/O banks and pads, tiles and sites, placed cells, Pblocks and (optionally) routing. The amount of detail grows with zoom; cells can be dragged onto sites to create LOC/BEL constraints or into Pblocks, and cell connectivity can be drawn for a selection.
tools.usage:
Window > Device (several Device windows can be open at once).
Toolbar: Previous, Next, Zoom In/Out/Fit, Select Area, Autofit Selection, Routing Resources, Draw Pblock, Cell Drag & Drop Modes (Create BEL Constraint / Create Site Constraint / Assign Cell to Pblock), Show Cell Connections (input/output, Max Cell Count), Settings (Layers, Colors, General).
Mouse strokes: drag top-left to bottom-right = zoom area, bottom-right to top-left = zoom fit, Ctrl+drag = pan; F9 fits the selection.

parameters.name: Layers
parameters.description: Design (cells, nets, ports, Pblocks) and Device (I/O banks, clock regions, tiles) layers can be toggled when the view is crowded or an object seems invisible.

parameters.name: General > Routing
parameters.description: When moving placed cells: leave existing routing, unroute branches, or unroute and reroute branches.

parameters.name: Autocheck I/O placement
parameters.description: Enforces I/O placement DRCs interactively while dragging ports.

tools.example:
open_run impl_1
# Colour the cells of a failing path and fit the view
set p [get_timing_paths -max_paths 1]
highlight_objects -color red [get_cells -of_objects $p]
select_objects [get_cells -of_objects $p]
# then press F9 (Auto Fit Selection) in the Device window
tools.notes: The World view (lower-right button when zoomed in) gives an overview navigator. Routing Resources on a large device is slow; zoom in first. Changes made by dragging cells are in-memory constraints until saved.

tools.name: Package window
tools.description: Physical ball-map view of the target package used for I/O planning: I/O banks are colour-coded, clock-capable pins are hexagons, user/multi-function pins circles, and VCC/GND pins power symbols. Ports are placed by dragging them from the I/O Ports window, and pin information cross-probes with the Device and Package Pins windows.
tools.usage:
Window > Package (normally part of the I/O Planning layout).
Toolbar: Previous, Next, Zoom In/Out/Fit, Select Area, Autofit Selection, Settings (Layers: I/O Ports, Pins, I/O Bank Types, I/O Banks, Other; General: Autocheck I/O Placement, Show Bottom View, Show Differential I/O Pairs).

parameters.name: Show Bottom View
parameters.description: Displays the package as seen from the PCB side (ball view), useful when cross-checking with board layout.

parameters.name: I/O Banks layer
parameters.description: Turning a bank layer off prevents assigning ports to it - a quick way to reserve or mark a bank full.

tools.example:
1. Open Elaborated or Synthesized Design, Layout > I/O Planning.
2. Drag port clk_100m from I/O Ports onto a clock-capable (hexagon) pin in the Package window.
# Echoed Tcl:
place_ports clk_100m E3
set_property IOSTANDARD LVCMOS33 [get_ports clk_100m]
tools.notes: A pin that is hidden by the layer settings cannot receive a port. Autocheck I/O Placement is on by default so only legal locations accept drops.

tools.name: Package Pins window
tools.description: Table of every package pin of the target part grouped by I/O bank, with bank type (High Performance / High Range / High Density), site type, differential-pair partner, min/max package trace delay (ps) and the port currently assigned. It is the tabular companion to the Package window for pin planning and for exporting pin data to the PCB team.
tools.usage: Window > Package Pins (part of the I/O Planning layout). Toolbar: Search, Collapse/Expand All, Group by I/O Bank, Settings > Scroll to Selected Objects. Editable cells accept typed or drop-down values; right-click > Export to Spreadsheet.

parameters.name: Min/Max package delay
parameters.description: Package trace delays in picoseconds, needed for length matching of high-speed interfaces.

parameters.name: Table colouring
parameters.description: Black = default, black with * = non-default, red = illegal value.

tools.notes: For a full pin list outside Vivado, write_csv exports package pins and port placement; the device's ASCII package file from the AMD website gives the same pin table without a design.

tools.name: I/O Ports window
tools.description: Table of the design's top-level ports (buses and interfaces as expandable folders) showing direction, board part pin/interface, package pin, I/O bank, I/O standard, drive, slew, diff-pair partner and voltage requirements. It is where ports are configured and placed (drag to Package/Device window, auto-place, place in bank/area/sequentially), fixed, swapped and exported as CSV, XDC, Verilog or VHDL.
tools.usage:
Window > I/O Ports (Layout > I/O Planning). Toolbar: Search, Collapse/Expand All, Group by Interface and Bus, Create I/O Port Interface, Schematic, Settings.
Right-click: I/O Port Bus Properties, Configure I/O Ports, Reset (Invalid) Port Properties, Set Direction / Make Diff Pair / Split Diff Pair (I/O planning projects), Auto-place I/O Ports, Place I/O Ports in an I/O Bank / in Area / Sequentially, Unplace, Fix Ports, Unfix Ports, Swap Locations, Highlight/Mark, Export I/O Ports, Export to Spreadsheet.

parameters.name: Fix Ports
parameters.description: Locks placed ports: set_property IS_LOC_FIXED true [get_ports ...].

parameters.name: Export I/O Ports
parameters.description: Writes the port list/assignments to CSV, XDC, Verilog or VHDL (the CSV is the usual exchange format with board designers).

parameters.name: Create I/O Port Interface
parameters.description: Groups ports into an interface that can be placed as one object.

tools.example:
# In an I/O Planning project (no RTL) import a CSV, then place and fix
read_csv ./board/pinout.csv
place_ports -iobank [get_iobanks 34] [get_ports {adc_d[*]}]
set_property IS_LOC_FIXED true [get_ports {adc_d[*]}]
write_csv -force ./board/pinout_placed.csv
tools.notes: Blank = default, * = non-default, red = illegal/undefined value. Unplaced ports are not shown in the Package window, only here. Run report_io and report_drc before signing off a pinout.

tools.name: Device Constraints window
tools.description: Small window for creating, editing and viewing bank-level device constraints: Internal VREF settings and DCI cascade chains. A drop-down at the top switches between Internal VREF and DCI Cascade; selecting two or more banks enables Add Constraint, which opens the Add DCI Cascade dialog to choose the master bank.
tools.usage: Window > Device Constraints. Toolbar: Search, Expand All, Collapse All, Add Constraint, Remove Constraint, Settings > Scroll to selected object.
tools.example:
# Tcl written by the window
set_property INTERNAL_VREF 0.75 [get_iobanks 33]
set_property DCI_CASCADE {32 34} [get_iobanks 33]
tools.notes: Banks can be selected from the Package Pins or Device windows. Internal VREF frees the VREF pins of a bank for user I/O when all inputs share one reference voltage.

tools.name: Hard Block Planner window
tools.description: Window (opened by default with a synthesized or implemented design on devices with hard IP) that collects the hard blocks of the design - GT quads, REFCLK pins and hard IP such as PCIe or integrated MACs - and lets you view or change their sites while cross-probing to the Device window. Columns show instance Name, Library Cell, Site, Fixed, Clock Region, Bank and REFCLK Source.
tools.usage: Open Synthesized/Implemented Design (opens automatically) or Window > Hard Block Planner. Toolbar: Search, Collapse/Expand All, Schematic, Show Hard-IP Connectivity, Show Hard-IP Connectivity for selected IP groups, Hide Hard-IP Connectivity.
tools.example:
1. Open Synthesized Design of a PCIe + GT design.
2. Hard Block Planner: select the GT quad row, change Site to the quad next to the REFCLK pins.
3. Show Hard-IP Connectivity to verify the REFCLK-to-quad relationship in the Device window.
4. File > Constraints > Save to write the LOC constraints.
tools.notes: Moving GT quads also moves which REFCLK pins are legal; check the transceiver IP's allowed locations and run report_drc afterwards.

tools.name: Selection window
tools.description: Lists every currently selected object (with a count in the banner) so you can verify, sort (Name, ID, Type), unselect or mark objects before acting on them. Selection itself follows the IDE rules: click, Ctrl+click, Shift+click ranges, Select Area and Ctrl+A, with secondary objects added according to Tools > Settings > Selection Rules.
tools.usage:
Window > Selection. Right-click: Unselect, Unselect All, Unselect All Except, Mark, Highlight.
Related: Tools > Settings > Selection Rules (enable/disable From->To secondary selection rules).
tools.example:
# The Tcl view of the same selection
set sel [get_selected_objects]
puts "[llength $sel] objects selected"
select_objects [get_cells -hier -filter {REF_NAME == BUFGCE}]
tools.notes: Unexpected extra objects in the selection (e.g. port pins when clicking a port, cells when clicking a Pblock) come from Selection Rules; disable the rule if it gets in the way.

tools.name: Manage Suppression / Message Severity (Messages window)
tools.description: GUI message control in the Messages window: right-click a message to Suppress this Message, Suppress Messages with this ID or Suppress Messages with this Severity, open Manage Suppression to add/remove text- or ID-based rules, or use Message Severity > Set/Unset Message Severity to promote or demote it. The Filter Messages toolbar button shows suppressed and/or modified-severity messages again.
tools.usage:
Messages window right-click: Suppress this Message | Suppress Messages with this ID | Suppress Messages with this Severity | Manage Suppression... | Message Severity > Set Message Severity / Unset Message Severity | Search for Answer Record
Toolbar: Filter Messages (Suppression: show suppressed/unsuppressed/both; Severity: show modified/unmodified/both), Manage Message Suppression, Discard User Created Messages, Settings (Group by File, Group by ID, Wrap Lines).

parameters.name: Manage Suppression dialog
parameters.description: Lists suppression rules; + opens New Suppression Rule (message ID or text string), - removes a rule.

parameters.name: Set Message Severity
parameters.description: Modified Information / Advisory / Warning / Critical Warning / Error; errors cannot be demoted.

parameters.name: Discard User Created Messages
parameters.description: Clears messages from project load, analysis and Tcl Console commands (not run messages - reset the run for those).

tools.notes: Suppressed messages carry a backslash through the icon when shown, modified ones an asterisk. In a project the rules are stored in a binary <project>.filter file next to the .xpr; for scripted builds keep set_msg_config calls in the script instead. The default per-ID display limit is 100.

tools.name: Log window and Reports window
tools.description: Two results-area windows: the Log window streams the output of synthesis, implementation and simulation for the active run (with a tree of out-of-context runs when present), and the Reports window lists the reports generated for the active run grouped by step, opening .rpt text in the Text Editor and interactive .rpx reports in their own windows. Additional reports are created on demand from the Reports menu or Flow Navigator.
tools.usage:
Window > Log (toolbar: Find, Pause Output, Copy, Toggle Column Selection Mode)
Window > Reports (toolbar: Search, Collapse/Expand All; double-click a report)
Reports menu: Report IP Status, I/O > Report Noise | Report I/O, Timing > Report Timing Summary | Report Bus Skew | Report Timing | Check Timing | Config Timing | Create Slack Histogram | Report Clock Interaction | Report CDC | Report Exceptions | Report Clock Networks | Report Pulse Width | Report Datasheet, Report Methodology, Report DRC, Report QoR Suggestions, Report QoR Assessment, Report Utilization, Report Clock Utilization, Report Power, Report Power Optimization, Report High Fanout Nets, Report Design Analysis; Reports > Open Interactive Report
tools.example:
# Run reports are files under the run directory:
ls ./proj.runs/impl_1/*.rpt
# Re-open the implementation timing summary interactively:
open_report -file ./proj.runs/impl_1/top_timing_summary_routed.rpx
tools.notes: Custom reports closed in the GUI are gone (re-run them); run-generated reports reopen via Reports > Open Interactive Report. Pause Output lets you scroll the Log while a run is still printing. Out-of-context run output is reached via Design Runs > Display Log/Reports/Messages.

tools.name: Report Timing Summary dialog and Timing window
tools.description: GUI front-end of report_timing_summary on an open synthesized or implemented design. The dialog's Options, Advanced and Timer Settings tabs choose delay type, paths per group, unconstrained paths, output file and timer settings (interconnect model, speed grade, multi-corner); results open in the Timing window with Design Timing Summary (WNS/TNS/WHS/THS/WPWS/TPWS), Clock Summary, Check Timing, Intra-Clock Paths, Inter-Clock Paths, Other Path Groups, User Ignored Paths and Unconstrained Paths.
tools.usage:
Reports > Timing > Report Timing Summary, or Flow Navigator > SYNTHESIS/IMPLEMENTATION > Report Timing Summary.
In results: click a path > Path Properties; right-click > Schematic (F4), View Path Report, Highlight/Mark (start green, end red, through yellow), Report Timing on Source/Destination.

parameters.name: Options tab
parameters.description: Report name, delay type (max, min, min_max), max paths per group / nworst, report unconstrained paths, path limits.

parameters.name: Advanced tab
parameters.description: Write the results to a text file (overwrite or append) in addition to the Timing window, plus less common report switches.

parameters.name: Timer Settings tab
parameters.description: Interconnect delay model (actual/estimated/none), speed grade and multi-corner configuration for what-if analysis without re-implementing.

tools.example:
# Tcl echoed by the dialog (typical)
report_timing_summary -delay_type min_max -report_unconstrained -check_timing_verbose -max_paths 10 -input_pins -routable_nets -name timing_1
# Scripted equivalent with files
report_timing_summary -max_paths 10 -file timing.rpt -rpx timing.rpx
tools.notes: The summary opened automatically with an implemented run is read-only; run the dialog again to change settings. Timer Settings changes affect later reports in the session until reset (config_timing_corners / set_delay_model).

tools.name: Text Editor (Vivado IDE)
tools.description: Built-in editor for Verilog/SystemVerilog/VHDL, XDC, Tcl, journal/log and plain text files with on-the-fly syntax checking (Sigasi-based for HDL), error markers beside the scroll bar, code completion (Ctrl+Space), Go to Definition, Find Usages, folding, block comments, whitespace operations, Find in Files / Replace in Files, file diff and Insert Template from the Language Templates.
tools.usage:
File > Text Editor > New File / Open File; double-click a source in the Sources window; File > Project > Open Log File / Open Journal File.
Toolbar: Find (Ctrl+F), Replace (Ctrl+R), Save, Undo/Redo, Cut/Copy/Paste, Toggle Line Comments, Toggle Column Selection Mode, Reformat Code, Language Templates, Settings.
Right-click: Go to Definition, Find Usages, Toggle Block Comments, Blank Operations, Diff with <file>, Folding, Insert Template, Find in Files.

parameters.name: Tools > Settings > Text Editor > Current Editor
parameters.description: Switch to an external editor (common editors are preset, or Custom Editor with your own command line); Vivado-editor-only options then disappear.

parameters.name: Syntax Checking
parameters.description: Enable/disable, show warnings/notes; the Sigasi cache lives under the user's Vivado data directory (e.g. ~/.Xilinx/Vivado/<ver>/sigasi-cache).

tools.example:
# When editing outside Vivado, check syntax from Tcl before running synthesis
check_syntax -fileset sources_1
# or a single file
check_syntax [get_files ./src/uart_rx.sv]
tools.notes: With a third-party editor there is no live syntax checking - run check_syntax manually. Diff requires both files open in the editor.

tools.name: Edit > Find (Find dialog, Ctrl+F)
tools.description: Property-based search for design or device objects in an open design: choose the object type (cells, nets, pins, ports, sites, BELs, clock regions...), add property conditions, optionally regular expression / ignore case / search hierarchically / Of Objects, and the dialog runs a get_* query wrapped in show_objects to fill a Find Results window. The Command field shows the exact Tcl, which makes it a good way to learn -filter syntax.
tools.usage: Edit > Find (Ctrl+F) with a design open. Fields: Results name, Find (object type), Properties (+/-), Regular expression, Ignore case, Search hierarchically, Of Objects (...), Command (preview), Open in a new tab.

parameters.name: Of Objects
parameters.description: Restrict the search to objects related to another object, e.g. BELs of a given SLICE site.

parameters.name: Open in a new tab
parameters.description: Keep previous Find Results instead of replacing them.

tools.example:
# Commands generated by typical Find dialog searches
show_objects -name unplaced_BUFGs [get_cells -hierarchical -filter { PRIMITIVE_TYPE == CLK.gclk.BUFG && STATUS == "UNPLACED" }]
show_objects -name placedBlockRAMB36 [get_sites -filter { SITE_TYPE =~ "RAMB36*" && IS_USED == "TRUE" }]
show_objects -name find_1 [get_cells -hierarchical -filter { IS_BLACKBOX == "TRUE" }]
tools.notes: get_* results are truncated to 500 entries in the console/log by default; the Find Results window shows all. In the Text Editor Ctrl+F is text search instead.

tools.name: Tools > Edit Device Properties
tools.description: Dialog for the device-level configuration and bitstream properties of an open synthesized or implemented design - configuration mode and voltage, SPI/BPI options, startup sequence, compression, encryption, readback and user ID settings. Hovering a value shows the underlying property name (e.g. Enable Bitstream Compression = BITSTREAM.GENERAL.COMPRESS), and OK applies set_property commands on the design.
tools.usage: Open Synthesized/Implemented Design > Tools > Edit Device Properties; pages are grouped by category (for example General, Configuration, Configuration Modes, Startup, Encryption, Readback). Then File > Constraints > Save to persist.
tools.example:
# Typical properties written by the dialog to the target XDC
set_property CFGBVS VCCO [current_design]
set_property CONFIG_VOLTAGE 3.3 [current_design]
set_property BITSTREAM.GENERAL.COMPRESS TRUE [current_design]
set_property BITSTREAM.CONFIG.SPI_BUSWIDTH 4 [current_design]
set_property CONFIG_MODE SPIx4 [current_design]
tools.notes: Changes are in memory only until File > Constraints > Save writes them to the target constraint file; forgetting this is why a regenerated bitstream 'loses' compression or SPI width. Project-level write_bitstream options live separately under Settings > Bitstream.

tools.name: Language Templates
tools.description: Browsable library of code templates for Verilog, SystemVerilog, VHDL and XDC: synthesis coding styles (RAMs, shift registers, FSMs, DSP inference), device primitive instantiation templates, Xilinx Parameterized Macro (XPM) instantiations, and constraint and debug constructs. A preview pane shows the template, and Insert Template drops it at the cursor in the Text Editor.
tools.usage: Tools > Language Templates; Flow Navigator > PROJECT MANAGER > Language Templates; or the Language Templates button in the Text Editor toolbar. Toolbar: Search (Alt+/), Collapse All, Expand All, Sort Alphabetically. In the Text Editor: right-click > Insert Template.
tools.example:
1. Tools > Language Templates.
2. Click Search (Alt+/) and type 'xpm_cdc_single' to locate the Verilog XPM CDC template.
3. Place the cursor in cdc_sync.v, right-click > Insert Template.
4. Replace the placeholder signal names and parameter values.
tools.notes: Templates track the installed release, so they are the quickest way to get the exact port list of a primitive or XPM for that version. The same templates exist as files in the installation, but the GUI is the supported way to browse them.

tools.name: Layout menu (Default Layout, I/O Planning, Floorplanning, Debug, Timing Analysis, ECO, Save Layout As)
tools.description: Predefined window arrangements for common tasks, selectable from the Layout menu or the layout selector in the main toolbar: Default Layout, I/O Planning (ports and package), Floorplanning (Pblocks, hierarchical floorplanning), Debug (debug nets and cores), Timing Analysis, and ECO (only when a checkpoint is opened). Custom arrangements can be saved and reset.
tools.usage:
Layout > Default Layout | I/O Planning | Floorplanning | Debug | Timing Analysis | ECO
Layout > Save Layout As... | Remove Layout... | Undo | Redo | Reset Layout (F5)

parameters.name: Save Layout As
parameters.description: Stores the current arrangement as a named user layout (a .layout file in the user's Vivado configuration directory).

parameters.name: Reset Layout (F5)
parameters.description: Restores the active layout's original window sizes and positions.

tools.example:
1. Open Synthesized Design.
2. Layout > I/O Planning (Package, I/O Ports and Package Pins windows appear).
3. Rearrange windows, then Layout > Save Layout As > 'my_pinout'.
4. Press F5 to reset if windows get lost.
tools.notes: In an I/O Planning project the I/O Planning arrangement is the Default Layout. Ctrl+Q hides/shows the Flow Navigator to gain space; double-clicking a window tab (or Alt+-) maximises it.

tools.name: Tools > Settings (Project Settings and Tool Settings)
tools.description: The central settings dialog. Project Settings (stored in the .xpr) cover General (part, top, language, extensible Vitis platform), Simulation, Elaboration, Synthesis, Implementation, Bitstream and IP; Tool Settings (stored per user) cover Project defaults, IP Defaults, Vivado Store, Source File, Display, Help, Text Editor, 3rd Party Simulators, Colors, Selection Rules, Shortcuts, Strategies and Window Behavior.
tools.usage: Tools > Settings, Flow Navigator > PROJECT MANAGER > Settings, the Settings toolbar button, or Edit next to Settings in the Project Summary.

parameters.name: Project Settings > General
parameters.description: Change part/board, top module, target language, 'Project is an extensible Vitis platform', and migrate pre-2020.2 projects to the .gen output-product layout.

parameters.name: Project Settings > Elaboration
parameters.description: Load the IP Netlist model (enables I/O planning of IP) or the faster Black box (stub) model.

parameters.name: Tool Settings > Project
parameters.description: Default project directory, target language, number of recent items, auto-open last project, 'Record Tcl commands for highlight and mark actions'.

parameters.name: Tool Settings > Display
parameters.description: Font scaling (OS or 90-300%), spacing (Comfortable/Compact), maximum messages, timing-report hyperlink action.

parameters.name: Tool Settings > 3rd Party Simulators
parameters.description: Install paths, GCC install paths and default compiled library paths per simulator (applied to new projects).

tools.example:
# Project-setting changes echo as properties, e.g.:
set_property target_language VHDL [current_project]
set_property STEPS.SYNTH_DESIGN.ARGS.FLATTEN_HIERARCHY none [get_runs synth_1]
set_property STEPS.WRITE_BITSTREAM.ARGS.BIN_FILE true [get_runs impl_1]
tools.notes: Tool Settings are saved per user to vivado.xml in the Vivado configuration directory when Vivado exits, so they are not part of a project archive. Grey fields are not applicable in the current context.

tools.name: Tools > Settings > Strategies (Run Strategies and Report Strategies)
tools.description: Pages for viewing the command-line options behind every predefined synthesis/implementation strategy and for creating user-defined run strategies and report strategies (which reports run at which step). Predefined strategies are read-only; Copy Strategy or Create Strategy makes an editable user version that then appears in run settings and the Design Runs Strategy column.
tools.usage: Tools > Settings > Strategies > Run Strategies | Report Strategies. Choose the Flow (Vivado Synthesis/Implementation <version>), then Create Strategy / Copy Strategy, set Name, Type, Tool Version, Description, and edit options or reports (Add Report: Run Step + Report Type).

parameters.name: User run strategy location
parameters.description: Windows %APPDATA%\Xilinx\Vivado\<version>\strategies ; Linux ~/.Xilinx/Vivado/<version>/strategies

parameters.name: User report strategy location
parameters.description: Windows %APPDATA%\Xilinx\Vivado\<version>\reportstrategies ; Linux ~/.Xilinx/Vivado/<version>/reportstrategies

tools.example:
# Apply strategies from Tcl
set_property strategy Performance_ExplorePostRoutePhysOpt [get_runs impl_1]
set_property report_strategy {Timing Closure Reports} [get_runs impl_1]
# A user strategy is referenced by the name given when it was created
set_property strategy MyTeam_Impl [get_runs impl_2]
tools.notes: Strategies are tool-version specific; user strategies must be recreated or copied when moving to a new release. In CI prefer explicit STEPS.* properties in the build script over per-user strategy files.

tools.name: Keyboard shortcuts (Tools > Settings > Shortcuts)
tools.description: Vivado ships a read-only 'Vivado Default' shortcut schema; to customise, copy it to a new schema and add or remove key bindings per command (and per window). Frequently used defaults: Ctrl+Q hide/show Flow Navigator, F4 Schematic, F5 Reset Layout, F6 Validate Design (IP Integrator), F9 Auto Fit Selection, Ctrl+F Find, Ctrl+R Replace, Ctrl+M Mark, Ctrl+H Highlight, Alt+/ in-window search, Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab switch workspace tabs, Alt+- maximise window, F1 Quick Help, Ctrl+Space code completion.
tools.usage: Tools > Settings > Shortcuts: Copy (new schema) > select command (Filter field) > Add > choose key > OK; Remove deletes a binding. To list current bindings deselect Group by Usage and sort by the Shortcut column.
tools.example:
1. Tools > Settings > Shortcuts > Copy > name 'mine'.
2. Filter 'Report Timing Summary' > Add > press Ctrl+Shift+T > OK.
3. Apply; the schema is saved to shortcuts/shortcuts.xml in the user Vivado configuration directory.
tools.notes: Custom schemas are per user and per Vivado version (…/Vivado/<version>/shortcuts). Shortcut keys shown next to menu items always reflect the active schema.

tools.name: Tools > Run Tcl Script
tools.description: Sources a Tcl script file into the running Vivado IDE session through a file browser, exactly as typing source <file> in the Tcl Console. Each executed line is echoed to the console and journal unless the script is sourced with -notrace.
tools.usage: Tools > Run Tcl Script... > browse to <script>.tcl > OK (echoes: source <path>/<script>.tcl)
tools.example:
# Equivalent console commands
source ./scripts/add_debug_cores.tcl
source ./scripts/reports.tcl -notrace
tools.notes: Relative paths inside the script resolve against the current working directory (pwd), which is the launch directory, not the script's directory; use [file dirname [info script]] inside scripts. For startup-time scripts use vivado -source or Vivado_init.tcl.

tools.name: Tools > Custom Commands > Customize Commands
tools.description: Dialog for adding your own entries to Tools > Custom Commands (and optionally toolbar buttons): each custom command has a Menu Name, Description, optional keyboard Shortcut, and either Run Command (a Tcl command or proc) or Source Tcl File, plus an optional toolbar icon. Commands persist per user across sessions.
tools.usage: Tools > Custom Commands > Customize Commands: Add / Remove / Move Up / Move Down; Edit Custom Command: Menu Name, Description, Shortcut (Add/Remove), Run Command | Source Tcl File, Toolbar Options: Add to the Toolbar, Icon File Path (PNG/JPG/GIF about 20x20).
tools.example:
1. Tools > Custom Commands > Customize Commands > Add > 'TimingNow'.
2. Run Command: report_timing_summary -max_paths 5 -name quick_ts
3. Tick Add to the Toolbar, choose an icon, OK.
4. The command appears under Tools > Custom Commands > TimingNow and on the toolbar.
tools.notes: Stored in commands/commands.paini under the user's Vivado configuration directory (%APPDATA%\Xilinx\Vivado\<version> or ~/.Xilinx/Vivado/<version>). The scripted equivalent is create_gui_custom_command, which is how Tcl Store apps add buttons.

tools.name: create_gui_custom_command / create_gui_custom_command_arg / remove_gui_custom_commands / get_gui_custom_commands
tools.description: Tcl API behind Tools > Custom Commands: create_gui_custom_command defines a menu item/toolbar button that runs a command or sources a Tcl file, create_gui_custom_command_arg adds arguments (prompted in a widget when the button is pressed), and remove_gui_custom_commands / get_gui_custom_commands / get_gui_custom_command_arg / remove_gui_custom_command_arg manage them. Placing these calls in Vivado_init.tcl gives a whole team the same buttons.
tools.usage:
create_gui_custom_command -name <unique_name> [-menu_name <text>] [-description <text>] [-show_on_toolbar] [-run_proc <true|false>] [-toolbar_icon <png_or_jpg>] [-command <tcl>] [-tcl_file <file>] [-quiet] [-verbose]
create_gui_custom_command_arg -command_name <name> -arg_name <name> [-default <value>] [-comment <text>] [-optional]
remove_gui_custom_commands <names>...
get_gui_custom_commands
get_gui_custom_command_arg / remove_gui_custom_command_arg

parameters.name: -name
parameters.description: Unique identifier without spaces; used to attach arguments and to remove the command.

parameters.name: -command / -tcl_file
parameters.description: Tcl command/proc to run, or script to source; with both given, -run_proc true selects the command.

parameters.name: -show_on_toolbar / -toolbar_icon
parameters.description: Add a main-toolbar button with the given image.

parameters.name: -optional (arg)
parameters.description: Argument may be left empty in the prompt widget.

tools.example:
create_gui_custom_command -name getClock -menu_name get_clock \
  -command {get_clocks -of [get_selected_objects]} \
  -description {Clocks through the selected objects} -show_on_toolbar
create_gui_custom_command -name showVersion -menu_name showVersion -description "Display the tool version" -show_on_toolbar -command version
remove_gui_custom_commands showVersion
tools.notes: Removing a command removes its arguments automatically. Guard creation with lsearch [get_gui_custom_commands] <name> in init scripts to avoid duplicate-name errors.

tools.name: Vivado Store (Tools > Vivado Store)
tools.description: In-tool catalog that consolidates three GitHub-backed stores: Tcl Apps (the Xilinx Tcl Store), Boards (XilinxBoardStore: AMD and third-party board files) and Example Designs (XilinxCEDStore: configurable example designs). Items are installed, updated or removed per user; a Refresh button per store updates its catalog, while the board files and examples shipped inside the installation cannot be uninstalled.
tools.usage: Tools > Vivado Store (also on the Getting Started page). Tabs: Tcl Apps | Boards | Example Designs; select an item > Install / Update / Uninstall; Refresh (lower left) updates the catalog. Download location: Tools > Settings > Vivado Store.

parameters.name: Download location
parameters.description: Default Linux ~/.Xilinx/Vivado/<ver>/xhub/board_store/, Windows %APPDATA%\Xilinx\Vivado\<ver>\xhub\board_store\ (configurable).

parameters.name: Board / Example Project Repository lists
parameters.description: Ordered search lists; when the same board or example exists twice, the first repository wins.

tools.example:
1. Tools > Vivado Store > Boards tab > Refresh.
2. Search 'kv260' > Install.
3. File > Project > New > Boards: the KV260 board part is now selectable.
# Scripted: see xhub::install
tools.notes: Behind a firewall the Refresh fails; use a local clone of the store repositories and set_param board.repoPaths instead. The first open shows a terms-of-use disclaimer.

tools.name: xhub::refresh_catalog / xhub::get_xstores / xhub::get_xitems / xhub::install / xhub::update / xhub::uninstall
tools.description: Tcl interface to the Vivado Store (board store and example-design store), used to install board files from scripts and CI instead of the GUI. get_xstores returns store objects (e.g. xilinx_board_store), refresh_catalog downloads the latest catalog, get_xitems lists installable items by pattern, and install / update / uninstall act on those items.
tools.usage:
xhub::refresh_catalog [xhub::get_xstores xilinx_board_store]
xhub::get_xitems [<pattern>]
xhub::install [xhub::get_xitems <pattern>]
xhub::update [xhub::get_xitems <pattern>]
xhub::uninstall [xhub::get_xitems <pattern>]
get_property LOCAL_ROOT_DIR [xhub::get_xstores xilinx_board_store]

parameters.name: xilinx_board_store
parameters.description: Store name for board files; item IDs look like <vendor>:xilinx_board_store:<board>:<version>.

parameters.name: LOCAL_ROOT_DIR
parameters.description: Property of a store giving the local directory where items are downloaded; add it to board.repoPaths when needed.

tools.example:
xhub::refresh_catalog [xhub::get_xstores xilinx_board_store]
xhub::install [xhub::get_xitems *kv260*]
set_param board.repoPaths [get_property LOCAL_ROOT_DIR [xhub::get_xstores xilinx_board_store]]
get_board_parts *kv260*
tools.notes: Requires internet access to GitHub; in air-gapped environments clone github.com/Xilinx/XilinxBoardStore and point board.repoPaths at the clone. Installed items are per user and per Vivado version.

tools.name: Xilinx Tcl Store (tclapp::install / tclapp::update / tclapp::uninstall)
tools.description: Open-source repository of community Tcl apps (e.g. xilinx::designutils, xilinx::projutils, xilinx::ultrafast, xilinx::profiler) that extend Vivado with new commands. Apps are installed from Tools > Vivado Store > Tcl Apps or with tclapp::install; installed procs register with help and are callable as ::<company>::<app>::<proc> (wrapper with -help/-verbose/-quiet) or ::tclapp::<company>::<app>::<proc>.
tools.usage:
tclapp::install <company>::<app>
tclapp::update <company>::<app>
tclapp::uninstall <company>::<app>
::<company>::<app>::<proc> [args] | ::<company>::<app>::<proc> -help

parameters.name: set_param tclapp.enableGitAccess 0
parameters.description: Disables catalog refresh (no queries outside the firewall); users get the static catalog shipped with the release.

parameters.name: XILINX_TCLAPP_REPO
parameters.description: Environment variable pointing Vivado at a local/cloned repository instead of GitHub (catalog refresh then disabled).

tools.example:
tclapp::install xilinx::designutils
xilinx::designutils::write_template -help
xilinx::designutils::write_template -verilog -cell u_fifo -file fifo_stub.v
tclapp::update xilinx::designutils
tools.notes: Install state and cached apps are kept per Vivado release under ~/.Xilinx (Linux) or %APPDATA%\Xilinx (Windows). Apps cannot be reverted to an older version, and the store does not track proc dependencies when viewing source.

tools.name: Tools > Associate ELF Files
tools.description: Associates a compiled software executable (.elf) with a MicroBlaze (or other BRAM-booted processor) instance so its code and data are merged into the block RAM initialisation of the bitstream, separately for Design Sources (synthesis/implementation) and Simulation Sources. It is the in-project alternative to running updatemem after the bitstream is built.
tools.usage: Tools > Associate ELF Files... > Design Sources / Simulation Sources > select processor (e.g. design_1_i/microblaze_0) > browse to app.elf > OK
tools.example:
# Tcl equivalent
add_files -norecurse ./sw/app.elf
set_property SCOPED_TO_REF design_1 [get_files -all -of_objects [get_fileset sources_1] ./sw/app.elf]
set_property SCOPED_TO_CELLS {microblaze_0} [get_files -all -of_objects [get_fileset sources_1] ./sw/app.elf]
launch_runs impl_1 -to_step write_bitstream
tools.notes: Changing the ELF marks the bitstream step out of date but not synthesis/placement. For fast firmware iteration without rerunning write_bitstream use write_mem_info + updatemem instead.

tools.name: Open Target > Auto Connect (Hardware Manager)
tools.description: One-click connection in the Hardware Manager: Auto Connect connects to the local hw_server (starting it on localhost:3121 if not running) and opens the first available JTAG target, populating the Hardware window with the device chain. Open New Target starts a wizard for a remote server, a specific cable, a Xilinx Virtual Cable URL or custom JTAG frequency.
tools.usage: Flow Navigator > PROGRAM AND DEBUG > Open Hardware Manager > Open Target > Auto Connect | Open New Target... | <recent targets>
tools.example:
# Tcl echoed by Auto Connect (typical)
open_hw_manager
connect_hw_server -allow_non_jtag
open_hw_target
current_hw_device [lindex [get_hw_devices] 0]
refresh_hw_device [current_hw_device]
tools.notes: If no target is found, check cable drivers (installed with the tools or separately), that only one hw_server owns the cable, and the board power. For Versal debug cores Vivado also uses cs_server (localhost:3042), started automatically when the default URL is used.

tools.name: Help > Add Design Tools or Devices
tools.description: Relaunches the AMD installer in 'add' mode so device families, tools (e.g. Vitis HLS, Vivado Lab, DocNav) or cable drivers that were deselected at install time can be added to the existing installation without reinstalling. It is the fix when a part is missing from the part selector or create_project reports that a part is not installed.
tools.usage: Help > Add Design Tools or Devices... (then follow the installer; administrative rights may be required for the installation directory)
tools.example:
# Symptom that calls for this menu:
#   ERROR: [Coretcl 2-106] Specified part could not be found.
get_parts xczu*   ;# empty -> Zynq UltraScale+ devices not installed
# Help > Add Design Tools or Devices > tick 'Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC' > Install
tools.notes: Device support is the largest part of the installation; install only needed families on build servers. After adding devices restart Vivado so the part list is reloaded.

tools.name: Documentation Navigator (DocNav)
tools.description: Standalone documentation browser installed with the tools that catalogs AMD user guides, data sheets, application notes, QuickTake videos and Design Hubs, with filtering, search, local download management and update notifications. Vivado's Help links and Getting Started documentation links can open documents in DocNav or in the web browser.
tools.usage: Windows: Start > Xilinx Design Tools > DocNav (or desktop icon); Linux: docnav. In Vivado: Help menu documentation links; choose DocNav vs browser in Tools > Settings > Help > Documentation. In DocNav: Catalog View, Design Hub View, Update Catalog.
tools.example:
docnav &
# then Catalog View > filter 'Vivado' + 'User Guides' > UG903 Using Constraints > Download
tools.notes: Old DocNav versions stopped opening documents after AMD moved hosting to docs.amd.com; update to 2022.1 or later. The same content is available online at docs.amd.com.

tools.name: Vivado License Manager (VLM)
tools.description: Utility for certificate-based licensing: it obtains licenses (opens the AMD Product Licensing site with this machine's host IDs pre-filled), loads a received .lic file into the default location, shows which license features are visible (View License Status), and on Windows sets license search paths (XILINXD_LICENSE_FILE / LM_LICENSE_FILE). It is the first stop when a licensed IP or Enterprise-edition device reports a license error.
tools.usage:
Vivado: Help > Manage License...; Windows Start menu 'Manage Xilinx Licenses'; Linux: vlm
Panes: Get License (Obtain License, Load License > Copy License), Manage License Search Paths (Windows only: set XILINXD_LICENSE_FILE / LM_LICENSE_FILE), View License Status, host/system information.

parameters.name: Load License > Copy License
parameters.description: Copies a .lic to %APPDATA%\XilinxLicense (Windows) or ~/.Xilinx (Linux), where the tools find it automatically.

parameters.name: Manage License Search Paths
parameters.description: Enter <port>@<server> (default port 2100) for a floating license; read-only on Linux, where the environment variable must be set in the shell.

tools.example:
# Linux: check what the tools see
vlm &                                  # View License Status
export XILINXD_LICENSE_FILE=2100@lic-server.example.com
vivado -mode tcl -source check_ip.tcl   # report_ip_status shows 'Licensed' per IP
tools.notes: Vivado ML Standard Edition and Lab Edition need no license. Host IDs (MAC address, disk serial, dongle) shown in VLM are what the licensing site binds node-locked licenses to.
